# <span id="aanchor63"></span> Ticket Types

The following ticket types are supported in FLOWCAL:

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Batch Meter">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Batch Meter</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Batch Meter">

Batch Meter tickets represent meter-measured product flow and contain a continuous record of meter operation. To view batch data, select "Batch Meter" in the Ticket Type selector. If you double-click a batch record in the grid, the Volume Editor will open and display the month containing that batch.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 615;height: 402;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Blow Down">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Blow Down</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Blow Down">

Blow Down tickets serve to indicate the quantity of a product lost by atmospheric venting. These tickets use FLOWCAL's API 12.2 Liquid Volumetric calculation. The calculation uses a K-factor, meter factor, and DFM of 1.0.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 616;height: 518;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Cavern">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Cavern Level</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Cavern">

Cavern Level tickets specify the amount of product contained within a cavern (inventory) at a given point in time.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Flare">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Flare</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Flare">

Flare tickets represent the amount of product burned off via flaring. These tickets use FLOWCAL's API 12.2 Liquid Volumetric calculation. The calculation uses a K-factor, meter factor, and DFM of 1.0.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 617;height: 520;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Tank Gauge">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Gauge Ticket</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Tank Gauge">

Gauge tickets specify the amount of product contained within a tank (inventory) at a given point in time.

Enabling the Gauge ticket type in FLOWCAL requires the Liquids Inventory module.

#### Upright cylindrical tank:



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 616;height: 488;" />

The Floating Roof Correction field label will change to Floating Roof Adjustment if the "FRA Built Into Table" option is selected in the tank capacity table.

#### Spherical tank:



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 617px;height: 504px;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Inventory Empty">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Inventory Empty</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Inventory Empty">

Enabling the Inventory Empty ticket type in FLOWCAL requires the Liquids Inventory module.

Inventory Empty tickets are created when an inventory empty operation is initiated for a liquid cavern; these tickets represent an event in which the entire inventory volume is reduced to 0. This is to match the calculated inventory in FLOWCAL to the actual reported empty from the field. A non-zero difference can result from measurement inaccuracies into and out of the tank or cavern.

Inventory Empty tickets cannot be edited manually, and they can only be created from the Liquid Cavern Editor. The data displayed is automatically calculated once the empty operation is performed and can only be changed by modifying data that will change the inventory prior to the empty operation (i.e., inventory data that has an effective date prior to the empty operation). When this data is modified, the Inventory Empty ticket will automatically revise the data, creating prior period adjustment records as necessary.

Inventory Empty tickets can only be closed by the [Meter Close service](../Services/All%20Services.md#MeterClose).



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 594;height: 515;" />

Hydrocarbon Inventory Empty Ticket



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 597;height: 518;" />

Non-Hydrocarbon Inventory Empty

The Allowable field is dependent upon which fluid service is assigned to the liquid cavern. Net Allowable is only available for hydrocarbon caverns and Mass Allowable is only available for non-hydrocarbon. The fluid service of the cavern is driven off of the product selection.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Meter">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Meter</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Meter">

Meter tickets measure product flow as indicated by a meter, similarly to Batch tickets. Unlike Batch tickets, however, Meter tickets represent one transaction at a given point in time.

The meter type and product specified control the display of certain fields on the Main tab. The calculation method, meter type and product will all affect the values expected and returned.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 615;height: 282;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Product Conversion">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Product Conversion</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Product Conversion">

Product Conversion tickets indicate an amount of product converted into another product (performed at the location level).

Product Conversion tickets may be created for tanks, liquid caverns, or standard locations, but require the following conditions to be met:

- The product to be converted must be flowing within the location of interest at the time a conversion is specified.
- The product to be converted must have a valid conversion product assigned to it within the product editor.
- The data for the location where the conversion is to occur must be rolled up.

Once these conditions are met, a Product Conversion ticket can be created by specifying the time of the conversion, the appropriate location, the product to convert from, the product to convert to, and the relevant measurement values for each product.

When a Product Conversion ticket is saved, each side of the conversion will appear as a distinct ticket, but each half will remain associated with the other. Any change to the common data within one of the tickets will apply to both tickets.

The "From" ticket will inherently have a direction of "Outlet" while the "To" ticket will have a direction of "Inlet".



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" />

Product Conversion tickets can be set up to have the pressure gauge type of either "Gauge" or "Absolute".  The Pressure Measurement Type and the Atmospheric Pressure can still be edited on each Product Conversion ticket if the default values are different for the "From" ticket or the "To" ticket.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 615;height: 278;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Rail Car">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Rail Car</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Rail Car">

Rail Car tickets represent the amount of fluid in a rail car at a given point in time.

The Level and Level Type fields function similarly to those seen for Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets, except there is no capacity table from which to derive a volume. The total observed volume must be manually specified to calculate the gross standard volume and mass. The fields in the right column are informational for display on printed tickets. The CTL will be calculated from the density and temperature provided. You may also manually input a CTL value, and the manually entered value will be used to calculate gross standard volume.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 614;height: 501;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Run">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Run Ticket</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Run">

Run tickets define the change in inventory of a tank due to a specific movement event.

#### Upright cylindrical tank:



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 587;height: 497;" />

The Extended Detail button is only visible if the "Open and Close Values for All Values" option is selected under Tank Characteristics.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Scale">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Scale</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Scale">

Scale tickets are used to quantify the intake or output of fluid indicated by a change in weight over the course of a transaction.

By specifying the weight in and weight out values, FLOWCAL can calculate the net weight of the transaction.

Along with the product's table type, the observed density, the observed temperature, and the net weight, FLOWCAL can calculate the gross standard volume. The net standard volume may be calculated using the gross standard volume and the S&W percent.

The Weigh In, Weigh Out, Out Scale ID, and In Scale ID fields are used to specify the times at which the movement started and ended.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 614;height: 415;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Vessel Tank">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Vessel Tank</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Vessel Tank">

Vessel Tank tickets capture the load (or unload) movement associated with a single tank located on a vessel.

Because vessels are transient, setting up a tank in FLOWCAL is not usually practical. Therefore, each Vessel Tank ticket completely specifies characteristics of the tank and calculations as well as the arrival and departure ullages and the load summary. Vessel Tank tickets can be attached to a location for balancing and accumulating inventory, but the ticket does not draw characteristic information from that location.

Vessel Tank tickets do not support a capacity table. Calculations start with a given Total Observed Volume (TOV). Levels can be provided for informational purposes but do not affect the calculations.

(See: [Vessel Tank Calculation Symbols](Vessel%20Tank%20Calculation%20Symbols.md) for a glossary of symbols associated with vessel tanks.)

Vessel Tank tickets support two calculation methods. API 12.1.2 (2012) is a volumetric calculation in that it calculates the volume of liquid first, then the mass of liquid. See Diagram 1. Mass is an inferred mass calculation that calculates the mass of liquid first, then the volume of liquid. See Diagram 2.

Vapor is always calculated as inferred mass, i.e., mass of vapor first, then volume of vapor.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 641;height: 339;" />



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 641;height: 386;" />

A prime feature of Vessel Tanks is the ability to validate third-party inspection reports. In practice, the inspector-provided reports, the arrival and departure ullages specifically, are brought in as vessel tank tickets. The ticket calculations are verified via correlation factors that are determined for each quantity. Vessel Tank tickets use a “Vessel” re-calc method for this purpose.

</div>
